a: XSS injects scripts into pages other users see; escape output and use CSP.
CSRF tricks a logged-in browser into unwanted actions; use tokens and SameSite cookies.
SQL injection alters queries via input; use parameterized queries.
IDOR accesses objects by guessing ids without authorization checks.
Never commit API keys; use env vars and secret managers.
HTTPS encrypts traffic in transit with TLS.
Grant only the minimum permissions needed.
Rate limits slow brute force and abuse.
Validate and constrain all untrusted input on the server.
Scan dependencies for known vulnerabilities regularly.
